what_happened: On a multi-lane freeway, with the route command STRAIGHT and then RIGHT, the policy took over at 4.7 s and steered left across the lane line, away from the recorded path. Its left side hit vehicle 41, which was coming up from behind in the adjacent left lane, at 6.2 s (a lateral collision).

On a straight multi-lane highway with a STRAIGHT command, after the 4.7s handoff the policy planned and started an unprompted lane change to the right. It cut into the right lane and its front hit actor 3, which was travelling next to it in that lane.

The ego was driving at about 6 m/s in the rightmost lane, next to the shoulder, while the road curved left. Its planned path (orange) went straight and then bent right instead of following the curve, and it drifted onto the dirt shoulder and off the road at 7.3 s, about 3.7 m from the human's path. The camera view was clean before the drift and no actor was involved.

The route command was RIGHT and the recorded human path curved right. Instead, the policy planned and drove a sweeping left, cutting diagonally across several lanes of a wide multi-lane road at about 5–6 m/s until it went off the drivable area at 8.9 s, 13.4 m from the recorded path. The metrics table shows only offroad (1.0) and no collision at any point, even though the input flags collision_at_fault and rear_ended; the camera is clear enough until the ego is well off the recording.

After handoff the route command was RIGHT, but the policy slowed from 17 to 7 m/s and steered left across the leftmost lane, leaving the road toward the sidewalk and storefronts, 11.8 m off the recorded path. As it crossed out at an angle, its right side touched actor 32, which was moving along the adjacent lane.

On a multi-lane highway, the ego kept to its lane and slowed from about 8 to 6.5 m/s. Actor 3, which had been in the lane to its right, moved left into the ego's lane right next to its front-right corner and made front contact at 6.5 s. The ego never turned right into it; its planned path stays in or left of its lane. In the recording, the human driver went right instead, so actor 3, which only replays its recorded path, cut in where the ego now was.

After handoff, the ego drifted left out of its lane while braking from about 20 to 11 m/s, even though the route command was STRAIGHT and then RIGHT and the recorded path stayed in the right lanes. It crossed the left lanes and ran onto the landscaped median before the intersection, ending about 7 m off the recorded path. The camera view was clean before it left the road.

The road and route curve left, but after handoff the ego kept going straight. It slowed from about 23 to 16 m/s and drifted over the right edge line onto the gravel shoulder next to the fence, ending about 2.6 m from the human's path. No other actors were involved, and the camera view stayed clean until the ego was already off the road.

In slow highway traffic, the ego drifted about 2.8 m right of the recorded path into the lane behind the slow grey van (actor 13). It then closed on the van (gap 8→4.4 m) and braked too gently (4.0→1.9 m/s), so its front hit the van's rear at 8.1 s. The rear contact on the ego came after this.

On a multi-lane highway with the route command STRAIGHT, the policy took over at 4.7s and started steering right toward the next lane (orange path), even though car 3 was driving alongside in that lane. By 6.4s the ego had turned into that lane, and its front hit car 3 at about 5.7 m/s. Car 3 was visible next to the ego the whole time.

On a multi-lane highway with the command STRAIGHT, the policy took over and planned a lane change to the right, toward the gap behind actor 4. Actor 3 was already traveling alongside in that right lane. The ego slowed from about 7.7 to 5.8 m/s and cut into the lane, and at 6.4 s its front-right struck actor 3, about 1.6 m off the recorded human path, which stayed in the original lane.

The road curved left, and the recorded human path curved with it. The ego slowed from about 23 to 16 m/s but kept heading straight and ran off the right edge onto the dirt shoulder by the fence. No other actor was involved.

In slow highway traffic with a LEFT command, the ego drifted right instead, ending up about 2.8 m right of the recorded path and in the lane of the silver van (actor 13). It slowed from 4.1 to 1.9 m/s, but too late, and its front hit the van's rear at 8.1 s; another vehicle later hit the ego's rear.

In slow highway traffic, the recorded human driver moved one lane left, but the ego stayed in its own lane about 3 m to the right of that path. It closed on the slow grey van ahead (actor 13) and hit its rear at about 1.6 m/s; it was slowing from 4.0 to 1.6 m/s, but not hard enough as the gap shrank from 7.6 m to 4.3 m.

After the 4.7 s handoff, the ego left the recorded straight path and steered right into the next lane while slowing gently from 7.7 to 6.5 m/s. Its front-right corner hit actor 3, which was in that lane just ahead and to the right. The route command was STRAIGHT and changed to LEFT at the end, so nothing called for a move to the right.

The ego was in the rightmost lane of a multi-lane road that bends gently left. Instead of following the bend (the route command changed from STRAIGHT to LEFT), it kept heading straight and drifted right onto the shoulder and dirt verge at about 6.5 m/s, ending 3.6 m off the recorded path. The camera view was clean before the drift, and there were no actors nearby that forced the move.

The ego was driving at about 6 m/s in the rightmost highway lane behind car 12 when the command said STRAIGHT and then LEFT. Its orange plan was already bending right at 5.2 s, while the camera view was still clean, and the ego drifted right over the edge line onto the dirt shoulder. It was off the road and 3.5 m from the human's path by 7.2 s, with nothing forcing it there.

The road curves left (the command switches to LEFT), but the ego kept heading straight while slowing from about 23 to 16 m/s. Its plan bent right, away from the curve, and it ran off the right edge onto the shoulder or sidewalk by the fence, about 2.5 m off the recorded path. There were no other actors nearby, and the camera view was clean before the failure.

After the 4.7s handoff the policy planned and steered a lane change to the right on the highway, away from the recorded path that stayed in lane. At 6.5s, going about 6.5 m/s, its front hit actor 3, a car beside it in the right lane.
